instruction: Select all images containing a hat.

game.semantic_variant: Select all things made to be worn on the head.
game.hint: Select all that apply. If you are unsure, use your best judgement.
game.explanation: Ordinary hats count, and so do the sunhat holding a duck pond and the bowler hat walking on legs: impossible, but still hats. The colander and the mushroom cap worn on the head are borderline cases, recorded without a verdict. The teacup, the plant pot and the lampshade are not hats.

correct: Hats identified. The Department doffs its own.
partial: Partially correct. A hat has blown away.
Partially correct. Some hats went unnoticed.
incorrect: Incorrect. Please keep this under your hat.
Incorrect. The Department will eat its hat, eventually.

selection_review.reason: Nine distinct, standardised images reviewed together at tile size: two ordinary hats (yellow baseball cap on white; pink bobble beanie on a fence post), two impossible hats (generated straw sunhat whose brim holds a pond with ducklings; generated bowler hat walking on trousered legs with no body), two borderline headwear items (generated man wearing a colander with a chin strap; generated woman wearing a giant mushroom cap) and three hat-shaped non-members (blue teacup on a saucer, terracotta plant pot, generated lampshade lying on a table). Rounded crowns and brims appear among targets, borderline cases and non-members alike, so shape alone does not decide. Views, colours and settings vary within each role. The bowler hat photograph, the white cap and the bicycle helmet worn as a hat remain in the collection for later versions.
